title: Segmented egress mirroring, time‑bounded upgrade contingency, and operator‑heartbeat acceptance for Private/VPC deployments
creator: Leah Chen
description:
Summary: Define requirements and acceptance criteria for a segmented egress mirroring feature and an accompanying time‑bounded upgrade contingency that ensures Private/VPC deployments (including air‑gapped and minimal‑egress customers) can safely receive operator-initiated upgrades. Include a lightweight operator heartbeat mechanism and delta artifact sync strategy to limit egress while preserving upgrade safety. This ticket scopes both requirements and acceptance criteria; implementation is tracked in ENG follow-ups.

Context and motivation: Many customers run Private/VPC deployments with restricted egress or scheduled egress windows. Current upgrade flows assume continuous access to our artifact mirrors or package repositories; when egress is unavailable upgrades stall or risk partial application. We need a predictable upgrade contract that: (1) limits egress footprint via segmented mirroring/delta syncs, (2) provides a strict time‑bounded contingency so upgrades either complete within a defined window or automatically rollback, and (3) exposes an operator heartbeat and health signals that allow us to distinguish a temporary egress outage from a full partition. This reduces operational blast radius and improves safety for regulated customers.

Scope (what this ticket covers):
- Requirements and acceptance criteria for segmented egress mirroring behavior (per‑site or per‑component artifact selection).
- Requirements for delta artifact sync to minimize bytes transferred for patch/upgrade sequences.
- Definition of a time‑bounded upgrade contingency window and automated rollback conditions.
- Operator heartbeat specification for air‑gapped/minimal egress sites (heartbeat channels, metrics, and tolerances).
- Required observability and runbook steps that must be present to mark the feature ready for private deploy customers.

Out of scope:
- End‑to‑end implementation details of kernel selection in the runtime (ENG will define).
- UI work for Console rollout controls (tracked separately under PM-xxxxxx Console rollout).

Nonfunctional constraints:
- For customers in restricted egress mode, the default upgrade artifact footprint must not exceed X MB per node for major upgrades and Y MB per node for minor patches (values defined in implementation doc—see links).
- Heartbeat overhead must be minimal: <5KB per 5 minutes per node and configurable.
- Contingency timers must be configurable per deployment but default to 2 hours for major upgrades and 30 minutes for minor patches.
acceptance_criteria: When segmented egress mirroring is enabled, the operator can declare one or more artifact mirror endpoints and a component segmentation map; during a staged upgrade only artifacts for targeted components are fetched (no full-image pulls unless explicitly allowed).

Delta sync must be supported for sequential upgrade operations: for a node that already has version N, the system must request only the delta from N->N+1 and not re-download the full artifact (testable with controlled checksums).

Upgrade process includes a time‑bounded contingency: if the upgrade does not reach successful state within the configured window, automated rollback is initiated and the deployment returns to the previous stable revision.

Operator heartbeat metric is emitted to local telemetry and to the control plane (when egress allowed) showing last successful heartbeat timestamp, last successful mirror contact, and cumulative bytes transferred during the upgrade. Heartbeat tolerances are documented and enforced.

For air‑gapped customers with scheduled egress windows, the upgrade flow must be able to operate in two modes: online delta sync (during window) and offline artifact staging (prepopulated media). Acceptance requires documented validation steps for both modes.

There are automated tests (integration and chaos) that simulate: (a) mirror unreachable during upgrade, (b) partial artifact delivery, (c) heartbeat dropouts, and verify rollback triggers and post‑rollback integrity.
Runbook and Console operator guidance exists and is linked in the ticket: steps to retry mirror sync, to force an offline artifact injection, and to safely override rollback under customer consent.
implementation_notes: Prefer using an index+delta format (content‑addressable) to allow small downloads for patches; avoid monolithic tarballs when delta is available.
Mirror segmentation map should be declarative YAML stored in operator config; segments map to logical subsystems (runtime, sidecars, model blobs).
The heartbeat should be a signed minimal JWT containing node ID, timestamp, and last applied revision to allow offline verification; do not include large telemetry payloads.
Tradeoffs: stronger guarantees require longer prefetch windows and more storage; documenting storage/retention tradeoffs is necessary for product guidance.
test_plan: Integration: Deploy a 3-node private cluster in a VPC with a simulated mirror; perform upgrades with segmented mirroring enabled and assert only segment artifacts are requested.
Delta test: Seed node with version A, perform upgrade to A+1 and assert bytes transferred are < 30% of full artifact size and checksums validate.
Chaos: During an upgrade, cut egress after 20% completion and validate that the contingency timer triggers rollback and cluster returns to stable state.
Airgap flow: Validate offline artifact staging via external media and run an upgrade with no egress; confirm operator heartbeat shows 'staged' status and node integrity post upgrade.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (Canary internal): Enable segmented mirroring for internal staging clusters with engineering opt‑in; validate metrics and tests (2 weeks).
Phase 1 (Early customers): Offer as opt‑in to selected Private/VPC customers with scheduled support and manual approval (4 weeks).
Phase 2 (General availability): Default behavior for new private deployments with config knobs exposed in operator and Console guidance (GA gated on reliability metrics).

2026-03-09 — Design feedback: Console should not expose artifact checksums by default for air‑gapped sites; link to design brief added.
